title: Remote Work's Hidden Cost: Isolation
hook: A new study finds people in fully remote jobs tend to be more socially isolated, anxious, and sad than those who aren't — but researchers say forcing everyone back to the office isn't the fix.
key_points: People in remote jobs reported more social isolation, anxiety, and sadness than people not working remotely.
Researchers stress this doesn't mean everyone should return to the office full-time.
The likely culprit is lost everyday social contact, not remote work itself.
Building deliberate connection — and some in-person time — may matter more than where you work.
content_html: Working from home is wildly popular — but a new study suggests it can quietly cost you. People in remote jobs reported being more socially isolated, anxious, and sad than people who weren't working remotely.
extra_html: The researchers are careful not to overreach: the answer isn't to drag everyone back to the office. The problem seems to be the loss of everyday social contact that an office supplies by default, not remote work itself. The practical takeaway is to build connection deliberately — regular check-ins, some in-person time, friendships outside work — rather than letting isolation accumulate. Reported by NPR.

related.title: Loneliness Is a Health Risk
related.hook: Chronic loneliness isn't just a bad feeling — it's linked to higher risk of heart disease, depression, and early death. And it's far more common than people admit.

related.title: Why Connection Matters
related.hook: Strong relationships aren't just nice to have — they predict how long and how well you live, on par with diet and exercise.

flashcards.explanation_html: Remote workers reported more isolation, anxiety, and sadness — but researchers say the answer isn't simply forcing everyone back to the office.

flashcards.prompt: Did the researchers conclude everyone should return to the office?
flashcards.back_html: No. They say the fix isn't forcing a return — it's replacing the everyday social contact remote work removes, through deliberate connection and some in-person time.

flashcards.prompt: What likely drives remote work's link to worse mood?
flashcards.back_html: The loss of the everyday, in-person social contact an office provides by default — not remote work itself.
